title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a manuscript page. It is a typed page from Grothendieck's SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'): page IX-63, with page number 381 at the bottom. It was filed among the 1976 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex, and the neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on that topic.

Setting: S is the spectrum of a henselian discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and residue characteristic p. A_K is an abelian variety over K, A its Néron model, A^o the identity component and A_o the special fibre. T_ℓ(A_K) = (ℓ^ν A_K)_ν is the ℓ-adic Tate module, viewed as a pro-group. ( )^f is the 'fixed part' of the quasi-finite S-groups ℓ^ν A, i.e. the largest sub-object that extends over S. The hypothesis that A^o is ℓ-divisible is automatic for ℓ ≠ p. For ℓ = p it means multiplication by p is an epimorphism on A^o.

Proposition 5.7: let F_K be a constructible ℓ-adic sheaf on K that is unramified, meaning it extends to a twisted-constant ℓ-adic sheaf F on S. Then every homomorphism of pro-groups u: F_K → T_ℓ(A_K) factors through T_ℓ(A_K)^f. In fact it extends to v: F → T_ℓ(A^o)^f.

Proof, level by level:
- Each F(ν) is étale, hence smooth, over S.
- By the Néron mapping property, u(ν): F_K(ν) → ℓ^ν A_K extends uniquely to v(ν): F(ν) → ℓ^ν A.
- By definition of the fixed part, v(ν) factors through (ℓ^ν A)^f.
- On the special fibre, v(ν) = ℓ^μ ∘ v(ν+μ) by compatibility. So its image is ℓ^μ-divisible for every μ, hence lies in the infinitely ℓ-divisible part of A_o.
- That part lies in the identity component, since the component group is finite. Hence v(ν) factors through (ℓ^ν A^o)^f.
- Pass to the limit over ν and restrict to the generic fibre.

Remark 5.7.2: for ℓ ≠ p this universal property characterises T_ℓ(A_K)^f as the largest unramified ℓ-adic subsheaf of T_ℓ(A_K), i.e. the inertia invariants T_ℓ(A_K)^I. For ℓ = p the statement 'ceases to be reasonable', and a different formulation follows on the next page (not present here).

The page serves the SGA 7 IX study of Néron models, monodromy and the semi-stable reduction criterion. It has no relation to the divided-power de Rham material on the adjacent pages; it is presumably a stray reprint or scrap sheet.
errors: No mathematical error. The step 'image of the special-fibre morphism falls into the infinitely ℓ-divisible part of A_o' is stated without proof. It follows from compatibility of the u(ν) with the transition maps, and the passage from the infinitely divisible part to A^o uses finiteness of the component group. Both points are left implicit.

ideas.what: Unramified ℓ-adic subsheaves of T_ℓ(A_K) extend over the Néron model and land in the fixed part of T_ℓ(A^o)
ideas.modern_name: Néron mapping property applied to Tate modules; inertia invariants T_ℓ(A)^I = T_ℓ of the identity component of the Néron model
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I Exp. IX (1967-69, publ. 1972); related to Serre–Tate (1968)
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, Prop. 5.7 and Remarques 5.7.2 (Lecture Notes in Math. 288, p. 381)

ideas.what: Characterisation of T_ℓ(A_K)^f as the largest unramified ℓ-adic subsheaf for ℓ ≠ p

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed page of published SGA 7 I Exp. IX (p. 381), apparently reused or misfiled among the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes. Its content is published and credited to Grothendieck. The only curiosity is archival: its unrelated placement in this folder.
transcription_corrections: Machine transcription is essentially accurate. Note that the page number '381' matches the pagination of SGA 7 I (LNM 288), confirming the identification as a printed or typed SGA page rather than a manuscript note.
In the proposition statement, 'S hensélien' refers to the base trait S; the factorisation target is T_ℓ(A_K)^f, as transcribed.
